text:
Roope Hintz scored twice for Dallas, the second time 3:47 into overtime, and the Stars beat Winnipeg 3-2 for their fourth straight win. The Jets, now winless in four (0-2-2), had led 2-1 in the second period before Hintz tied it with two seconds left... or rather at 18:00 of the third, his snap shot making it 2-2. Jason Robertson, who assisted on both of Hintz's goals, also reached 500 career points.

The game was played mostly in Winnipeg's end. Dallas took 60 shot attempts to 41 and 38 shots on goal to 19. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, favored Dallas 4.32 to 3.08, and the Stars deserved to win 69 percent of the time (the share of simulated replays of every shot that they would take). Winnipeg's only stretch of control came in the second period, when it scored twice in under two minutes through Gabriel Vilardi and Kyle Connor, and Connor had the best chance that didn't go in, a 39 percent look in overtime that Jake Oettinger stopped. Neither power play scored, with Winnipeg 0 for 4 and Dallas 0 for 2.

Stuart Skinner is the reason the Jets were in it. He faced 38 shots and saved about 1.3 goals more than the quality of those chances suggested he would. Miro Heiskanen played 29:18 for Dallas and was on the ice for 2.85 expected goals for against 0.75 against. Dallas leaves with four straight wins. Winnipeg gets a point for the overtime loss but still has no win in its last four games.
